historical_references.reference: Deveedaas was a title given to the Jain monk Gautama Mahavira during his lifetime. The term 'Deveedaas' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Deva' meaning god and 'Daas' meaning servant. Mahavira was considered a god-like figure by his followers and was therefore referred to as 'Deveedaas'.

The Hindu god Shiva is also known by the name 'Deveesha' or 'Deveesa', which means 'Lord of the Gods'. This name is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures such as the Shiva Purana and the Bhagavata Purana. The god Shiva is considered the supreme deity in the Hindu pantheon and is thus referred to as 'Deveesha'.
